title: Italy’s estate agents report weaker demand and fewer homes coming to market
summary: Italian estate agents reported that the rise in selling prices lost momentum in the third quarter of 2026. The share reporting price increases exceeded the share reporting falls by only 0.9 percentage points, down from 7.0 points in the previous quarter and 7.1 a year earlier. This is a balance of opinions about transactions handled by agencies. It does not say that national house prices rose by 0.9%. The joint survey by Banca d’Italia, Tecnoborsa and the Revenue Agency covers about 1,500 agencies interviewed from 14 September to 21 October. Its value is in showing where the negotiation changed before subsequent transaction-price statistics arrive (pp. 1–2, 6).

Buyers were scarcer, but owners also brought fewer homes to market. Agencies reporting a decline in potential buyers outnumbered those reporting an increase by 20 percentage points, compared with 15 points the previous quarter. For new instructions to sell, the negative balance widened to about 33 points. With supply and demand both weakening, lower activity need not translate into an equivalent price fall. Some 83.2% of agencies completed at least one sale, against 85.8% a year earlier. The net share reporting higher rather than lower sales year on year was about minus 23 points. That describes the breadth of the decline across agencies, without measuring its size in transaction units (pp. 2, 4, 6, Figure 3).

Buyers secured a little more room to negotiate. The average discount to the seller’s asking price reached 7.7%, up from 7.1%, while the share of deals at or above the asking price fell from 17% to 11%. Average marketing time rose from 5.2 to 5.5 months. Both the discount and time to sale remained low in the longer history shown in Figure 2. The geography matters to valuations. The net balance for selling prices remained positive at 10 points in the North-East, where discounts averaged about 6%. It fell to minus 9 points in the South and islands, where discounts were around 10%. A national average would conceal the different amounts a seller could realise from similar asking prices (pp. 1–3).

Mortgages financed 69% of completed purchases, against 63% in the second quarter, the highest share since mid-2022. The year-on-year increase mostly reflected urban markets. Loan-to-value ratios remained close to 78%. The higher mortgage share could reflect a change in the mix of buyers or a decline in cash purchases. In a market with fewer transactions, it does not establish that banks originated more loans or loosened standards (pp. 2, 4, 6, Figure 4).

Rental and owner-occupied markets sent different signals. The balance of agents reporting rising rents was about 34 points, down seven points from a year earlier. In cities of more than 500,000 people it dropped eleven points to 23. Instructions to rent remained scarce and landlords conceded only about 2% against asking rents. Respondents’ assessment of the national market over the following two years weakened from minus 10 to minus 21 points. These expectations add a forward-looking measure of sentiment. Actual rents, sale prices and loan performance will depend on how many prospective tenants and buyers transact at the new terms (p. 3).

questions.question: Is the weaker price balance visible in completed sales after adjusting for the type and location of properties?
questions.detail: An estate agent counts equally in the balance whether prices changed slightly or substantially. The shift may also reflect the mix of homes sold. Compare later official transaction counts and house-price indices with tax-agency records by location and property type. Persistent declines in realised prices and increasing time to sale in the same districts would matter more for collateral valuations than a nationwide change in opinion alone.

questions.question: Did mortgage-financed purchases rise in number as well as in share?
questions.detail: The survey records financing of completed deals and a nearly unchanged loan-to-value ratio. It does not observe rejected applications or the number of cash purchases outside the surveyed agencies. Compare subsequent mortgage originations, approval rates, transaction registrations and lending standards. For banks, an increase in the numerator would have different implications for new business and borrower risk than a contraction in cash purchases.

questions.question: Can constrained rental supply sustain rents in the regions where sale prices are weakening?
questions.detail: New instructions to rent declined and agreed rents stayed close to asking levels, but the rental balance slowed most in large cities. Examine newly registered rental contracts, vacancy and listing duration by city, separating new leases from renewals. That would show whether achievable rents still support property income when capital values and transaction liquidity come under pressure.
